data.narrative:
MacroFab is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $141M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable set of nine firms (one public, eight private) operating in the same sector and stage cohort, including peers such as Exotec, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Hadrian.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $141M total raised proxy, implying a valuation of $240M. Peer-median methodology references seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.6B and a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B, directly implying $1.6B. The wide dispersion between methods reflects the heterogeneity within the robotics cohort—stage variance among peers (Series B through Series D) and likely differences in revenue maturity and capital efficiency.

The triangulated analysis produces a range from $204M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $945M. The stage-progression method yields a conservative floor anchored to historical capital deployment; peer comparables anchor the upper end. Key uncertainties include MacroFab's revenue run rate and path to profitability relative to the peer set, the degree to which stage differences among comparables should discount or premium the median, and whether robotics subsector focus (logistics, manufacturing automation, hardware-enabled services) materially differentiates valuation. A mid-range placement of $500M–$800M may be more defensible pending detailed operational metrics.
